figures.finding: A minor's contracts to repay money lent, for goods other than necessaries, and accounts stated are absolutely void, and no action lies on a promise made after full age to pay a debt of minority; other contracts stand as the common law or another Act lets a minor make them (the Act says so), so a contract of service for performing, writing or directing is left to the common law, not read here; no share of earnings is set aside by any Act found.

figures.finding: There is no permit for a child performer; the general Act reaches performing work only through its bars: a child (under sixteen) may not be employed in an industrial undertaking or on a ship, may not work between 6 p.m. and 7 a.m. in any undertaking whatever, and no one may employ a child or young person of compulsory school age during school hours. A film or stage production isn't an industrial undertaking as the Act defines it (mines, manufacture, building and civil engineering, transport), so a child may act outside school hours and before 6 p.m. (reading); the same reaches a child writer or director employed on set.

figures.finding: No one under eighteen may form or join in forming a company, and anyone so barred may not be a director.

figures.finding: The National Cultural Foundation's Cultural Industries Development Fund, which covers film production, is open to all citizens of Barbados and to Barbadian-registered companies whose principal shareholder or partner is a citizen, provided the applicant has registered on barbadosartists.bb; it states no applicant age.
